extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: An environment for training software engineering agents containing 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42nd Intemational Conference on Machine Leaming
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection involved using SEART GitHub search to filter initial repositories, extracting task instances using SWE-Bench's script, and semi-automatically collecting versions. Executable environments were then manually configured and validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world software engineering tasks sourced from pull requests in 11 popular open-source Python repositories on GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation. Instances were then validated using an execution-based script, and failed instances were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotators manually configured dependencies for each task instance to create executable environments, which required approximately 200 human annotation hours.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench's instance extraction script and SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility, but may impact software engineering jobs, require careful consideration around code ownership, and could potentially be misused to automate malicious code creation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a long-tail repository distribution (e.g., pandas comprises nearly one-third of tasks). There is also a potential distribution bias if environments are ignored, and a bias toward easier tasks during trajectory sampling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training language models as software engineering agents and verifiers.
